problem_statement: Contiki-NG has no process-level mutex. A protothread that needs exclusive access to a shared resource cannot attempt to acquire a lock and, when the lock is already held, defer until it is released and then be automatically resumed; the only existing alternative (sys/pt-sem.h) does not wake a waiting protothread on release. A user needs a way to initialize a mutex and then try to lock it: the attempt should succeed immediately when the lock is free and fail (recording the caller as a waiter) when it is already held; releasing the lock should wake a waiting protothread and clear the lock, and when more than one protothread is waiting the release must wake all of them so the lock can be re-tried. Required behavior: an initialized (zeroed) mutex can be acquired at once; a held mutex rejects a try-lock and queues the waiter; an unlock clears the lock and posts the wake event to the waiting process(es). This is the interface the new test uses: an initialization step, a try-to-lock step, and an unlock step, with one and two contenders contending for the same mutex.

verification.reason: The statement describes the required behavior but omits the exact public API names, header path, and return type needed by the hidden test. These can be added without revealing the implementation.

problems.detail: The hidden test uses the exact public names process_mutex_t, process_mutex_init, process_mutex_try_lock, and process_mutex_unlock, but the statement only describes the operations generically.
The hidden test includes sys/process-mutex.h, so the public header path is part of the required interface and must be stated.
The two-contender behavior depends on unlock clearing the recorded waiter state after waking, not only clearing the locked state; the statement does not make this explicit.

leak_check.leak_detail: The phrase 'This is the interface the new test uses' mentions the tests. The API and behavioral details are allowed, but the test mention should be removed.
leak_check.suggested_statement: Contiki-NG has no process-level mutex. A protothread that needs exclusive access to a shared resource cannot attempt to acquire a lock and, when the lock is already held, defer until it is released and then be automatically resumed; the only existing alternative (sys/pt-sem.h) does not wake a waiting protothread on release. A user needs a way to initialize a mutex and then try to lock it: the attempt should succeed immediately when the lock is free and fail (recording the caller as a waiter) when it is already held; releasing the lock should wake a waiting protothread and clear the lock, and when more than one protothread is waiting the release must wake all of them so the lock can be re-tried. Required behavior: an initialized (zeroed) mutex can be acquired at once; a held mutex rejects a try-lock and queues the waiter; an unlock clears the lock, clears any recorded waiter(s), and posts the wake event to the waiting process(es). The required interface consists of an initialization step, a try-to-lock step, and an unlock step, with one and two contenders contending for the same mutex. The public interface must be provided by sys/process-mutex.h and must define a process_mutex_t type plus functions process_mutex_init(process_mutex_t *mutex) returning void, process_mutex_try_lock(process_mutex_t *mutex) returning bool, and process_mutex_unlock(process_mutex_t *mutex) returning void. process_mutex_try_lock returns true only when it acquires the mutex, and false when the mutex is already held and the current process has been recorded as a waiter.
